threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the number 73 bus is a quick way to get to the city—wait till you're stuck behind a school run and the inevitable traffic.
Last night on the 196, a guy was arguing with his reflection in the window, convinced it was a rival. We all just pretended to look out.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh currywurst wafting through the Sunday market, as kids chase pigeons and the old man feeds them from his pocket. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's not unusual to find a kebab shop open at 4 AM serving late-night dancers returning from Berghain, a true testament to Berlin's nightlife culture.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they know to avoid the Civic Center BART station after 6 PM—never a good sign when smoke starts billowing.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 31 Balboa, tapping his foot to music only he could hear. Just another Tuesday in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can find authentic Catalan food near the Sagrada Família, but you’ll only get frozen paella and view selfies.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their bright white sneakers. Locals know that a little scuff goes a long way in this city.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by how they still rave about the 'lovely' market at Chatsworth Road, while locals roll their eyes at the overpriced artisan bread.
Last Friday on the 35, two blokes argued over a lost phone; it turned into a karaoke showdown to 'find it'. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a hidden kiosk selling homemade baklava, I realized Neukölln is full of little treasures, just waiting to be discovered.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar that doubles as a library. Grab a beer and browse through hundreds of books while waiting for your drink.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they dodge the BART delays like it’s an Olympic sport. Tourists just stand and stare at the screens.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo quietly napping on the 14, only to wake up and start singing opera when the bus hit a bump. Classic Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just for Gaudí, but the real heart beats in the small plaça bars where locals gather after work, not in the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll notice them struggling with the metro ticket machines, pressing buttons like it's a game show and still ending up lost on the wrong line.
